items.title: 63475_Arnett Cobb oral history interview
items.q: we played the Fillmore Auditorium in San Francisco on Easter Sunday with James Brown, Leslie Hawkins -- who is getting big now -- Arnett Cobb, band backing them up

ctx.x: Yeah. See, Ben didn't die until I come back to Houston. He died in 1966. I come back to Houston in '59. Ben dropped dead on the golf course in Miami, and Jack, his son, was walking with him when he died. See, they had a boat house down there in Miami, and Maxine and he lived -- spent a lot of time down there, and then he had trained for the office and Jack (inaudible) Jack had taken over mostly. When Ben go in, on what to do he'd give him instructions (inaudible), but he was more or less retired.

But what happened to Ben, James Brown didn't [resign] that contract, and he made a lot of money off of James. See, I brought James Brown to him. He asked me to screen him out in Georgia. Clint was his manager, the guy that had brought us for the show, package show. I was with the Five Royals at the time.

And Ben said, "I want you to put him on and tell me what you think about him." This is Macon, Georgia. Well now, we had intermission, and I come back and open up the Five Royals. [Don Eddy] closed the first half of the show. So I played one tune and brought James Brown and the Five Flings
